extracted.intended_audience: researchers and policymakers using patent data (economists, innovation scholars, patent analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and empirical investigation into how to define and measure 'patent quality', comparing common post-grant outcome measures and grant-time patent indicators and assessing their consistency and variation across technologies and stakeholder viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-dimensional view of patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting that different stakeholders have different views of this concept, we take a multi-dimensional view of patent quality in this work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent quality should not be treated as a single scalar construct; analysts should consider multiple dimensions that reflect differing stakeholder perspectives when defining or measuring quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of popular post-grant outcomes as patent quality measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper tests the consistency of popular post-grant outcomes that are often used as patent quality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly-used post-grant outcomes (e.g., outcomes observable after grant) are widely used as proxy measures of quality, but the authors find these measures to be generally inconsistent; therefore reliance on any single post-grant outcome as a definitive quality measure is problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-time patent indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a raft of patent indicators that are defined at the time of grant to dissect the characteristics associated with different post-grant outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators observable at grant (bibliographic/filing/claim characteristics, examiner/subject-matter attributes, etc.) can be used to analyze which grant-time features are associated with later outcomes, but their predictive importance varies by outcome and technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and sensitivity of patent quality measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of patent quality is highly sensitive to both stakeholder viewpoint and technology type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and policymakers should check for sensitivity and lack of robustness when using patent quality proxies: a measure that correlates with one stakeholder's notion of quality or one technology area may not generalize to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity in importance of individual characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: There is broad disagreement in the relative importance of individual characteristics between outcomes and significant variation of the same across technologies within outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing or interpreting patent quality metrics, explicitly allow for heterogeneity — both across different post-grant outcomes and across technology classes — rather than assuming uniform effects of patent features.
